$comment: What this SDK actually does. `supported` means the contract suite exercises it; `not_supported` is a real gap stated in the SDK's own voice; `planned` is accepted work not yet landed. scripts/gen-sdk-matrix.mjs renders clients/README.md's capability table from these three files and CI diff-checks the result, so a README can no longer promise a feature one language does not have.

notes.span: The builder emits only on send(); there is no timed span type, so latency is caller-measured.
notes.journal: No crash-surviving breadcrumb. A Rust process killed mid-call leaves no record of it, where the Python and TypeScript clients would recover one. This is a gap, not a design choice - clients/catchup-marker.json has carried it as a flagged debt since 2026-08-24.
notes.instrument: No provider-SDK wrapping. Rust provider clients are third-party and un-monkey-patchable; instrumentation would need per-crate adapters.
notes.relay: No relay client. Enqueue tasks over plain HTTP against /v1/relay/tasks (docs/RELAY.md).
notes.admit: Pre-spend admission: `Client::admit()` / `Client::gate()` with `Client::enforce("block" | "warn" | "off")`, default off. There is no instrument wrapper to gate here (see above), so the caller invokes the gate itself. The shed lottery calls straight through to lighttrack_core::shed_ticket - the server's own function.
